description: The North American Rail Network (NARN) is the Federal Railroad Administration's geographic database of the railway system of the United States, Canada and Mexico, created in 2016 and published in the National Transportation Atlas Database. The lines layer, last updated on 21 July 2026, held 302,771 segments on 26 September 2026 and the nodes layer 250,202 nodes that make the network routable. Each segment records up to three owning, operating or maintaining railroads, up to nine holders of trackage rights, division, subdivision and branch, yard name, passenger service, membership of the Strategic Rail Corridor Network (STRACNET), number of tracks, network status, length and state and county codes, mapped at 1:24,000 or better within the United States. Views by Class I railroad (BNSF, CN, CPKC, CSX, NS, UP) and for passenger rail are also published. The data are served as ArcGIS feature services (JSON, GeoJSON, PBF) with downloads, and as a US government work they are free for unrestricted public use; the data dictionary has DOI 10.21949/1528950. Caveats: accuracy outside the United States is lower, ownership fields describe several distinct roles, and the network shows track alignments, not capacity or traffic. NARN is used for freight rail routing, network flow and hazard exposure studies, and it is related to the NTAD record and underlies the BTS rail hazard exposure layers.
